;==============================================================
; MSRT.LST - the runtime that LINK /Q puts into a QuickLibrary
;==============================================================

; Disassembly of the part of the runtime that Microsoft's linker
; (LINK 3.69, switch /Q) takes from BQLB45.LIB of QuickBASIC
; 4.50 and puts into every QuickLibrary: the modules ultort.asm,
; erbcproc.asm and ulutil.asm, which are the dispatcher behind
; b_ULVars[0] and the thunks of the QuickBASIC services. The
; annotations are ours (DosWorld 2026, public domain); the
; instruction bytes are Microsoft's, so check the rights before
; you redistribute this file.

; How it was made: a small object was linked with LINK /Q
; ARBO.OBJ,MS.QLB,NUL,BQLB45.LIB; the three modules were located
; in the code image of MS.QLB by comparing their bytes with the
; OMF records of BQLB45.LIB. Names and offsets are the public
; symbols of that library; the listing is ndisasm output with
; labels. Statements marked "inferred" are read from the code
; and were not run.

; Reading it
;   Offsets are offsets in the code segment of the runtime
;   (the segment that the symbol CODE of the QLB names). A far
;   call "0x2c:0x2f5" goes to the same code segment (relocated
;   segment word); "0x0:" is the _TEXT segment of the C
;   runtime part of the library. [0xNN] with DS is a variable
;   in the data segment of QuickBASIC (list below). The
;   selector table is the one of DOC\QLB-IMP.MD section 8.

; Variables of the QB data segment (ulstart.asm, segment NULL),
; the offsets that DS-relative code of a library can use.
; RLINK knows these names as imports (DOC\QLB-IMP.MD section 9).

;   0000 STKHQQ                0000 __anullsize
;   0002 __aaltstkovr          0006 __asizds
;   0008 __atopsp              000A __aexit_rtn
;   000C __abrktb              005C __abrkp
;   005C __abrktbe             005E __acfinfo
;   006A b$cfilex              006B __aintdiv
;   006F __fac                 0077 _errno
;   0079 __umaskval            007B __pspadr
;   007D __psp                 007F __osversion
;   007F __dosvermajor         007F __osmajor
;   0080 __dosverminor         0080 __osminor
;   0081 __osmode              0082 __oserr
;   0082 __doserrno            0084 __nfile
;   0086 __osfile              009A ___argc
;   009C ___argv               009E _environ
;   00A0 __child               00A2 __pgmptr
;   00A8 __acmdln              00AA __acmdseg
;   00AC __aenvseg             00AE __ovlflag
;   00AF __intno               00B0 __ovlvec
;   00B4 b$pend                00B6 b$pendchk
;   00B8 b$pBC_SAB             00B8 __bpBC_SAB
;   00BA b$nmalloc_start       00BC b$nmalloc_end
;   00BE b$pULtoRTFar          00C2 b$pULtoRTNear
;   00C6 b$Chaining            00C6 b$RTMOverlayStart
;   00C7 b$chaindata_len       00C9 b$seg
;   00CB $AC                   00CB $DAC
;   00CB B$DAC                 00CF B$AC
;   00D3 b$ULSymSeg            00D3 b_ULSymSeg
;   00D5 b$ULDataLength        00D7 b$ULDataStart
;   00D9 b$FHDULNearData       00E1 b$FHDULFarData
;   00E9 b$CtrlFlags           00EA b$userflags
;   00EC b$mainframe           00EE b$curframe
;   00F0 b$curlevel            00F2 b$EVTRETV
;   00F6 B$VALTYP              00F6 b$VTYP
;   00F7 b$TTYP                00F8 b$LPTFDB
;   00FE b$PUDS                0102 b$erradr
;   0102 b_erradr              0106 b$errmod
;   0106 b_errmod              010A b$errnum
;   010A b_errnum              010C b$errlin
;   010C b_errlin              010E b$inonerr
;   010F b$PTRFIL              0113 b$cCSubs
;   0115 b$cNonQBIFrames       0117 __aseglo


;==============================================================
; module ultort.asm  (cs:00A8..01B7)
; user library to runtime: error thunks, the entry
; b_ULVars[0] (B$RTtoULFar), thunks of QB services
;==============================================================

; B$ERR_NOL: BX = 9400h, then the common raise code.
B$ERR_NOL:
  00A8  BB 00 94     mov bx,0x9400
  00AB  E9 B7 00     jmp B$RUNERR

; B$ERR_BFM .. B$ERR_OV: eight entry points, each sets BL
; (the "mov bl,N" is hidden inside the next "cmp ax,imm"):
; BFM 54, IFN 52, DV0 11, FC 5, RG 3, OM 7, AFE 73, OV 6.
; BH = 0, then raise the error.
B$ERR_BFM:
  00AE  B3 36        mov bl,0x36
  00B0  3D B3 34     cmp ax,0x34b3
  00B3  3D B3 0B     cmp ax,0xbb3
  00B6  3D B3 05     cmp ax,0x5b3
  00B9  3D B3 03     cmp ax,0x3b3
  00BC  3D B3 07     cmp ax,0x7b3
  00BF  3D B3 49     cmp ax,0x49b3
  00C2  3D B3 06     cmp ax,0x6b3
  00C5  32 FF        xor bh,bh

; raise a run-time error: BX = error code; B$RUNERR does not
; return to the caller.
L00C7:
  00C7  E9 9B 00     jmp B$RUNERR

; B$ERR_OSS: BX = 9007h.
B$ERR_OSS:
  00CA  BB 07 90     mov bx,0x9007
  00CD  EB F8        jmp L00C7

; B$RTtoULNear: call near [cs:DI+0EAh], retf.
B$RTtoULNear:
  00CF  81 C7 EA 00  add di,0xea
  00D3  2E FF 15     call word near [cs:di]
  00D6  CB           retf

; B$RTtoULFar = b_ULVars[0], the entry of the library.
; CX = selector 0,2,..,10h. Jumps through the table at cs:00EC
; (below). The handler ends with RETF (selectors 0..6) or
; RETF 2 (selectors 8..10h) and returns to QuickBASIC.
B$RTtoULFar:
  00D7  81 C1 EC 00  add cx,0xec
  00DB  8B D9        mov bx,cx
  00DD  2E FF 27     jmp word near [cs:bx]

; gateway to QuickBASIC, near form: call far [DS:00C2]
; (b$pULtoRTNear). DI = service number. DS must be the QB
; data segment. Every thunk below ends here.
L00E0:
  00E0  FF 1E C2 00  call word far [0xc2]  ; b$pULtoRTNear
  00E4  5F           pop di
  00E5  C3           ret
        ; gateway, far form: jmp far [DS:00BE] (b$pULtoRTFar).
        ; BX = service number.
  00E6  FF 2E BE 00  jmp word far [0xbe]  ; b$pULtoRTFar

; services of QuickBASIC, numbers 0,2,..,42. Each thunk:
;    push di / mov di,N / jmp gateway (call far [DS:00C2],
;    pop di, ret). The far entry points of the group below
;    use "mov bx,N / jmp far [DS:00BE]".
B$BREAK_CHK:
  00FE  57           push di
  00FF  BF 00 00     mov di,0x0
  0102  EB DC        jmp L00E0

B$FOUTBX:
  0104  57           push di
  0105  BF 02 00     mov di,0x2
  0108  EB D6        jmp L00E0

B$LHLOCFDB:
  010A  57           push di
  010B  BF 04 00     mov di,0x4
  010E  EB D0        jmp L00E0

B$RES_SETUP:
  0110  57           push di
  0111  BF 06 00     mov di,0x6
  0114  EB CA        jmp L00E0

B$TYPUI:
  0116  57           push di
  0117  BF 08 00     mov di,0x8
  011A  EB C4        jmp L00E0

B$LHFDBLOC:
  011C  57           push di
  011D  BF 0A 00     mov di,0xa
  0120  EB BE        jmp L00E0

B$$WCLF:
  0122  57           push di
  0123  BF 0C 00     mov di,0xc
  0126  EB B8        jmp L00E0

B$$RCH:
  0128  57           push di
  0129  BF 0E 00     mov di,0xe
  012C  EB B2        jmp L00E0

B$$TCR:
  012E  57           push di
  012F  BF 10 00     mov di,0x10
  0132  EB AC        jmp L00E0

B$$WCH:
  0134  57           push di
  0135  BF 12 00     mov di,0x12
  0138  EB A6        jmp L00E0

B$STALCTMP:
  013A  57           push di
  013B  BF 14 00     mov di,0x14
  013E  EB A0        jmp L00E0

B$TTY_SOUT:
  0140  57           push di
  0141  BF 16 00     mov di,0x16
  0144  EB 9A        jmp L00E0

B$STDALC:
  0146  57           push di
  0147  BF 18 00     mov di,0x18
  014A  EB 94        jmp L00E0

B$STDALCTMP:
  014C  57           push di
  014D  BF 1A 00     mov di,0x1a
  0150  EB 8E        jmp L00E0

B$STDALCALLTMP:
  0152  57           push di
  0153  BF 1C 00     mov di,0x1c
  0156  EB 88        jmp L00E0

B$PUTNUM:
  0158  57           push di
  0159  BF 1E 00     mov di,0x1e
  015C  EB 82        jmp L00E0

__BRUNERR:
  015E  57           push di
  015F  BF 20 00     mov di,0x20
  0162  E9 7B FF     jmp L00E0

B$RUNERR:
  0165  57           push di
  0166  BF 22 00     mov di,0x22
  0169  E9 74 FF     jmp L00E0

B$FHHighAlloc:
  016C  57           push di
  016D  BF 24 00     mov di,0x24
  0170  E9 6D FF     jmp L00E0

B$FHHighDealloc:
  0173  57           push di
  0174  BF 26 00     mov di,0x26
  0177  E9 66 FF     jmp L00E0

B$IFHAlloc:
  017A  57           push di
  017B  BF 28 00     mov di,0x28
  017E  E9 5F FF     jmp L00E0

B$FHDealloc:
  0181  57           push di
  0182  BF 2A 00     mov di,0x2a
  0185  E9 58 FF     jmp L00E0

; far group (BX = 0,4,..,20): B$ULReload, B$IStop, B$END,
; B$GetNmalloc, B$IEND, B$SetUEvent.
B$ULReload:
  0188  BB 00 00     mov bx,0x0
  018B  EA E6 00 2C+ jmp word 0x2c:word 0xe6

B$IStop:
  0190  BB 04 00     mov bx,0x4
  0193  EA E6 00 2C+ jmp word 0x2c:word 0xe6

B$END:
  0198  BB 08 00     mov bx,0x8
  019B  EA E6 00 2C+ jmp word 0x2c:word 0xe6

B$GetNmalloc:
  01A0  BB 0C 00     mov bx,0xc
  01A3  EA E6 00 2C+ jmp word 0x2c:word 0xe6

B$IEND:
  01A8  BB 10 00     mov bx,0x10
  01AB  EA E6 00 2C+ jmp word 0x2c:word 0xe6

B$SetUEvent:
  01B0  BB 14 00     mov bx,0x14
  01B3  EA E6 00 2C+ jmp word 0x2c:word 0xe6

;==============================================================
; module erbcproc.asm  (cs:01B8..0221)
; B$CONERR: hands a run-time error to QuickBASIC
;==============================================================

; B$CONERR (selector 08h, one word argument): hands a run-time
; error to QuickBASIC while library code is active.
; Details: DOC\QLB-IMP.MD section 8.3.
B$CONERR:
  01B8  55           push bp
  01B9  8B EC        mov bp,sp
  01BB  33 C0        xor ax,ax
  01BD  E8 4A FE     call L000A
  01C0  C7 06 06 01+ mov word [0x106],0x2  ; b$errmod
  01C6  89 1E 08 01  mov [0x108],bx
  01CA  A1 0A 01     mov ax,[0x10a]  ; b$errnum
  01CD  80 3E 0E 01+ cmp byte [0x10e],0x0  ; b$inonerr
  01D2  75 4A        jnz L021E
  01D4  0A E4        or ah,ah
  01D6  75 46        jnz L021E
  01D8  C6 06 0E 01+ mov byte [0x10e],0xff  ; b$inonerr
  01DD  8B 5E 06     mov bx,[bp+0x6]
  01E0  8B 47 02     mov ax,[bx+0x2]
  01E3  8B 57 04     mov dx,[bx+0x4]
  01E6  A3 02 01     mov [0x102],ax  ; b$erradr
  01E9  89 16 04 01  mov [0x104],dx
  01ED  52           push dx
  01EE  E8 85 FE     call L0076
  01F1  A3 0C 01     mov [0x10c],ax  ; b$errlin
  01F4  5A           pop dx
  01F5  1E           push ds
  01F6  8E DA        mov ds,dx
  01F8  8B 1E 0E 00  mov bx,[0xe]
  01FC  1F           pop ds
  01FD  8B 5F 04     mov bx,[bx+0x4]
  0200  87 CB        xchg cx,bx
  0202  E3 1A        jcxz L021E
  0204  8B 5E 06     mov bx,[bp+0x6]
  0207  8B 2F        mov bp,[bx]
  0209  8B C5        mov ax,bp
  020B  2B 46 F8     sub ax,[bp-0x8]
  020E  2B 46 F6     sub ax,[bp-0xa]
  0211  2B 46 F6     sub ax,[bp-0xa]
  0214  2D 0A 00     sub ax,0xa
  0217  8B E0        mov sp,ax
  0219  52           push dx
  021A  51           push cx
  021B  E9 09 FE     jmp L0027

L021E:
  021E  5D           pop bp
  021F  CA 02 00     retf word 0x2

;==============================================================
; module ulutil.asm  (cs:0222..057D)
; GETPROC, GETCOMMON, GetData, GetSeg, Init, Term,
; AllocDataImage, DataRelease
;==============================================================

; B$ULGetCommon (selector 10h, one word argument).
; Argument: near pointer to a name descriptor, or 0 (then the
; name is "COMMON"). Looks the name up in the SEGMENT table
; (bl = 0Ch) and answers the offset and size of the area in
; BX and DX; AX = BX = DX = 0 if there is none.
B$ULGetCommon:
  0222  55           push bp
  0223  8B EC        mov bp,sp
  0225  06           push es
  0226  8B 5E 06     mov bx,[bp+0x6]
  0229  0B DB        or bx,bx
  022B  74 06        jz L0233
  022D  83 7F 02 00  cmp word [bx+0x2],0x0
  0231  75 05        jnz L0238

L0233:
  0233  C7 46 06 46+ mov word [bp+0x6],0x3346

L0238:
  0238  B3 0C        mov bl,0xc
  023A  FF 76 06     push word [bp+0x6]
  023D  9A F5 02 2C+ call word 0x2c:word 0x2f5
  0242  0B C0        or ax,ax
  0244  75 04        jnz L024A
  0246  0B D2        or dx,dx
  0248  74 29        jz L0273

L024A:
  024A  51           push cx
  024B  E8 FA 00     call L0348
  024E  5B           pop bx
  024F  50           push ax
  0250  8E 06 D3 00  mov es,word [0xd3]  ; b$ULSymSeg
  0254  83 C3 08     add bx,0x8
  0257  26 C4 47 04  les ax,word [es:bx+0x4]
  025B  8C C2        mov dx,es
  025D  E8 E8 00     call L0348
  0260  92           xchg ax,dx
  0261  58           pop ax
  0262  2B D0        sub dx,ax
  0264  76 0A        jna L0270
  0266  3D 6E 33     cmp ax,0x336e
  0269  75 08        jnz L0273
  026B  83 FA 06     cmp dx,0x6
  026E  77 03        ja L0273

L0270:
  0270  33 C0        xor ax,ax
  0272  99           cwd

L0273:
  0273  93           xchg ax,bx
  0274  33 C0        xor ax,ax
  0276  07           pop es
  0277  5D           pop bp
  0278  CA 02 00     retf word 0x2

; B$ULGetProc (selector 0Ah). Argument [bp+6]: near pointer
; to the BASIC string descriptor {length, pointer} of the
; name.
; DX = flag: 0040h for a CDECL declaration, else 0.
; Answer: far address in DX:AX, 0:0 if the name is unknown.
B$ULGetProc:
  027B  55           push bp
  027C  8B EC        mov bp,sp
  027E  83 EC 04     sub sp,0x4
  0281  8B 46 06     mov ax,[bp+0x6]
  0284  0B D2        or dx,dx
  0286  74 28        jz L02B0
        ; flag <> 0: name := "_" + name (string
        ; concatenation),
        ; then every "." of the new string becomes "_".
  0288  B1 5F        mov cl,0x5f
  028A  51           push cx
  028B  8B DC        mov bx,sp
  028D  B9 01 00     mov cx,0x1
  0290  53           push bx
  0291  51           push cx
  0292  8B DC        mov bx,sp
  0294  53           push bx
  0295  50           push ax
  0296  9A 42 02 00+ call word 0x0:word 0x242
  029B  83 C4 06     add sp,0x6
  029E  8B D8        mov bx,ax
  02A0  8B 0F        mov cx,[bx]
  02A2  8B 5F 02     mov bx,[bx+0x2]

L02A5:
  02A5  80 3F 2E     cmp byte [bx],0x2e
  02A8  75 03        jnz L02AD
  02AA  C6 07 5F     mov byte [bx],0x5f

L02AD:
  02AD  43           inc bx
  02AE  E2 F5        loop L02A5

; the name (or the new string) is assigned to the local
; string variable [bp-4]; this takes over the temporary string
; of QuickBASIC (inferred). The routine frees it at the end
; with
; B$STDALC.
L02B0:
  02B0  8D 5E FC     lea bx,[bp-0x4]
  02B3  C7 47 02 00+ mov word [bx+0x2],0x0
  02B8  50           push ax
  02B9  53           push bx
  02BA  9A 3F 02 00+ call word 0x0:word 0x23f
        ; BL = 8: look in the CODE table (offset +08h of the
        ; QB
        ; header) with the lookup routine at 02F5.
  02BF  B3 08        mov bl,0x8
  02C1  50           push ax
  02C2  9A F5 02 2C+ call word 0x2c:word 0x2f5
        ; found (DX <> 0): done. Else look in the DATA table
        ; (BL=0Ah):
  02C7  0B D2        or dx,dx
  02C9  75 19        jnz L02E4
  02CB  8D 5E FC     lea bx,[bp-0x4]
  02CE  53           push bx
  02CF  9A F0 02 2C+ call word 0x2c:word 0x2f0
        ; accept only an address whose segment is not below
        ; w1, the
        ; code base (word +0Eh of the QB header, relocated);
        ; otherwise answer 0:0.
  02D4  06           push es
  02D5  8E 06 D3 00  mov es,word [0xd3]  ; b$ULSymSeg
  02D9  33 DB        xor bx,bx
  02DB  26 3B 57 0E  cmp dx,[es:bx+0xe]
  02DF  07           pop es
  02E0  73 02        jnc L02E4
  02E2  93           xchg ax,bx
  02E3  99           cwd

; free the string variable [bp-4]: B$STDALC.
L02E4:
  02E4  8D 5E FC     lea bx,[bp-0x4]
  02E7  E8 5C FE     call B$STDALC
  02EA  8B E5        mov sp,bp
  02EC  5D           pop bp
  02ED  CA 02 00     retf word 0x2

; B$ULGetData (selector 0Ch): BL = 0Ah (DATA table); the
; "cmp ax,0CB3h" hides "mov bl,0Ch" = entry of B$ULGetSeg
; (selector 0Eh, SEGMENT table); both fall into the lookup.
B$ULGetData:
  02F0  B3 0A        mov bl,0xa
  02F2  3D B3 0C     cmp ax,0xcb3
        ; lookup(table, name): BL = 8 CODE, 0Ah DATA, 0Ch
        ; SEGMENT
        ; (index into the QB header: the offset of the table
        ; is the
        ; word at [b$ULSymSeg:BX]). The name is first copied
        ; and
        ; upper-cased by a runtime routine (call 0:0281). Each
        ; entry
        ; {flags, name offset, offset, segment} is compared
        ; with
        ; repe cmpsb; the stored name must end (byte 0) where
        ; the
        ; name ends. Found: ES:AX = the address, CX = the
        ; entry.
        ; The temporary copy is freed with B$STDALCTMP at the
        ; end.
        ; The stored names were upper-cased by QB when it
        ; loaded the
        ; library, so the compare ignores case.
  02F5  55           push bp
  02F6  8B EC        mov bp,sp
  02F8  56           push si
  02F9  57           push di
  02FA  06           push es
  02FB  32 FF        xor bh,bh
  02FD  53           push bx
  02FE  FF 76 06     push word [bp+0x6]
  0301  9A 81 02 00+ call word 0x0:word 0x281
  0306  5B           pop bx
  0307  50           push ax
  0308  96           xchg ax,si
  0309  33 C0        xor ax,ax
  030B  99           cwd
  030C  8E 06 D3 00  mov es,word [0xd3]  ; b$ULSymSeg
  0310  8B 0C        mov cx,[si]
  0312  8B 74 02     mov si,[si+0x2]
  0315  26 8B 1F     mov bx,[es:bx]
  0318  83 EB 08     sub bx,0x8

L031B:
  031B  83 C3 08     add bx,0x8
  031E  26 83 3F 00  cmp word [es:bx],0x0
  0322  74 19        jz L033D
  0324  26 8B 7F 02  mov di,[es:bx+0x2]
  0328  51           push cx
  0329  56           push si
  032A  F3 A6        repe cmpsb
  032C  5E           pop si
  032D  59           pop cx
  032E  75 EB        jnz L031B
  0330  26 38 05     cmp [es:di],al
  0333  75 E6        jnz L031B
  0335  26 C4 47 04  les ax,word [es:bx+0x4]
  0339  8C C2        mov dx,es
  033B  8B CB        mov cx,bx

L033D:
  033D  5B           pop bx
  033E  E8 0B FE     call B$STDALCTMP
  0341  07           pop es
  0342  5F           pop di

mrsaraiva-alleycat-portable-src-docs-sta.text:
# Portable C port: current status and remaining work

Status: playable, with full gameplay and execution-time parity still unproven.
Updated: 2026-10-04.

## Implementation

The supported runtime translates the original ASM routines into the `dos_*.c`
modules listed in CMake. NASM assembles the original data declarations and the
build generates the initial relocated data segment. The game draws a live
320×200 CGA framebuffer; its startup prompts and gameplay screens come from
translated routines and source data.

The desktop host uses SDL3 for video, audio, keyboard and joystick. The browser
host runs the same core in a WebAssembly worker with keyboard input, canvas
presentation and Web Audio. Neither target needs a DOS executable or emulator
at runtime. The [ASM reconstruction](../../src/README.md) is the behavioral
reference, while host scheduling and hardware adapters are port responsibilities.

## Current functionality

| Area | Current coverage |
| --- | --- |
| Startup and shell | Title, control/difficulty prompts, alley, window/room entry, results, game over and return routes. |
| Rooms | Fish collection, spider/fern, cheese, cage/bird, kennel and Felicia reward routines are translated and playable. |
| Progression | Reported ordinary-input comparisons cover base-difficulty room successes and six consecutive Felicia rewards, reaching difficulty 6 with seven lives. Coverage of later play is incomplete. |
| Failure recovery | Reported comparisons cover base-difficulty last-life failures and selected nonterminal failures at higher difficulties. Every room/difficulty combination is not covered. |
| Rendering | Source-driven CGA page, sprites, underlays, score digits, palette and BIOS text. The IBM PC AT BIOS text table covers bytes `0x00–0x7F`; extended teletype characters are unsupported. |
| Controls | Original keyboard prompts, movement, Alt action, pause, sound toggle, restart, menu and exit. Desktop joystick input includes calibration and virtual-device coverage; browser input is keyboard only. |
| Audio and clocks | Shared PIT/BIOS/speaker model and source tone routines. Original whole-game speed and audio timing are not established. |

## What is left

1. **Execution-time fidelity.** Model whole-shell instruction pacing and IRQ/PIC
   latency against an explicit reference hardware profile. Presentation and
   host load can change tone counts and RNG progression in timing-sensitive
   source loops. Matching deterministic hardware observations does not prove
   physical DOS speed or sound timing. Browser scheduling adds another timing
   policy that needs independent acceptance.
2. **Progression beyond the accepted routes.** Cover the difficulty-six fern
   route, later progression and room selection, and sustained play without
   resets. Reported success through the sixth Felicia reward is a bounded route,
   not proof of all levels.
3. **Failure combinations.** Extend ordinary-input coverage across remaining
   room hazards, difficulties, nonterminal life loss and last-life returns.
   Verify the complete room/result/alley sequence, not only a terminal flag.
4. **Physical devices and platforms.** Verify actual controllers, disconnect
   and replacement behavior, native Windows/macOS operation and execution-time
   behavior on intended hardware. Virtual-device checks and Wine runs have
   narrower scope than physical native acceptance.
5. **Other hardware profiles.** PCjr/composite presentation remains unsupported.
   The current CGA RGB and IBM keyboard scope should stay explicit until those
   configurations have implementation and independent evidence.

## Verification available in this repository

The documented desktop CMake configuration registers nine checks for clocks,
gameport, BIOS video, host timing, SDL keyboard/hotkeys, virtual controller
behavior and startup/control smoke routes. Core-only and WebAssembly builds
register three hardware/renderer checks.

On 2026-10-04, fresh public-source builds passed all nine desktop checks and
all three WebAssembly checks. A browser smoke check reached the alley through
the normal prompts with no observed browser errors. These checks establish
bounded build/runtime behavior, not complete gameplay, physical-controller or
original-speed parity. See [build and test instructions](../README.md).

The instruction-level comparisons in `tests/oracle/` and capture tools in
`tools/oracle/` need a separately supplied
original DOS image and their stated tooling prerequisites. That image and
complete comparison-run artifacts are not distributed here. The gameplay
comparisons summarized above are reported acceptance coverage, not results
reproduced by the three or nine CMake checks.

When extending acceptance, use ordinary input from cold start and preserve
state through room returns and reward transitions. State injection, isolated
subsystem passes and matching retained screenshots alone do not establish
ordinary-play completion. Record the exact source revision, configuration,
route and observed state when reporting new coverage.

bstar-pcplus-recomp-analysis-pcplus-eval.text:
# PCPlus reassessment and reconstruction status

The REA/Ghidra decompilation route works. A controlled incremental reconstruction
is practical; a complete source rebuild is still unfinished. The earlier stop
for supposedly missing Ghidra/Java was unnecessary: an existing installation was
present but invisible to the connected MCP process. Analysis now uses a pinned
Nix environment and an actual REA 6.5.0 stdio MCP connection.

## Artifacts and measured coverage

| Work | Result | Evidence/artifact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Preserve inputs | Three original executable variants plus a complete 32-file copy of the active install | `pcplus-originals/SHA256SUMS`, `pcplus-install/inventory.json` |
| Verify original MZ import | 4,608 header bytes, 53,456 initialized module bytes, 155,952 appended bytes; relocation and mapping checks passed | `pcplus-main/inspect_native_load_image.json`, Evidence `ev_e64adede842cb5581a5caa88c7267b5fe09e200a2aa6cbcc31d7beee9f04e6ab` |
| Resident decompilation | 515 pseudocode files and matching assembly exports | `pcplus-main/functions`, overview Evidence `ev_a333d7c28a07e193e7b0b27f687521d56f71c40c309349d54d7396301f170519` |
| Parse PLINK86 overlays | 31 code overlays and one startup-data overlay, every file boundary validated | `inspect_pcplus.py`, `pcplus-overlays/manifest.json` |
| Seed overlay analysis | 502/502 unique exported entrypoints discovered in their respective overlay contexts | `pcplus-overlay-anchored-summary.json` |
| Export overlay functions | 894 pseudocode functions plus assembly, zero failed tool operations | `pcplus-overlay-anchored-01` through `pcplus-overlay-anchored-31` |
| Reassemble serial code | UART block (466 instructions, 1,099 bytes) plus 46-byte receive timeout; 1,145 unique bytes rebuilt exactly | `../reconstruction/uart/core.asm`, `../reconstruction/uart/receive_timeout.asm`, candidate manifest |
| Compile a DOS program | Nix-built Open Watcom successfully compiled an MZ DOS compiler probe; flake checks passed | `../nix/flake.nix`, check `dos-compiler` |
| Build compatibility candidate | Two serial source units inserted into the original container; 214,016 bytes, exactly two changed bytes; eight handler cases passed | `../reconstruction/dist/tech-net-candidate/manifest.json` |
| Exercise full DOS application | Startup/compiler, UART terminal queries, CSI-q regression, keyboard and exit checks pass; raw serial and emulated Hayes/Telnet | `../reconstruction/lab/*/result.json`, `../reconstruction/dos_lab.py` |

Function counts are exports in specified analysis contexts, not a claim that
every original source function or type has been recovered. Known exported-entry
coverage is measured against the program's own 502 trampoline entries. All
native sessions created by the analysis clients were closed.

The complete install copy includes private dialing/configuration data. It is
kept locally for later testing and is not an input to the Nix package derivation.

## Version choice

Both 214,016-byte PCPlus 2.01 executables contain identical resident code and
identical code overlays. Their only differences are ten contiguous bytes in
startup data overlay 32. There is no different code patch level to choose
between these copies. The active install is a suitable reproducible baseline.
The older 1.1B binary is retained for reference, not selected for development.
No original PCPlus source project or original compiler/linker build files were
found in the inspected installation.

## A concrete terminal lockup and a tested candidate

The preserved [Datastorm support archive](https://aspectscripting.com/support.shtml)
contains `TECH_NET.DTP`, which describes keyboard lockups associated with
`ESC [ ; 4 q`. The original patch recipe is retained in
`archived-support/dp201/tech_net.dtp`; its source archive URL and hash are in
`archived-support/manifest.json`. Archives were extracted with Lhasa; their DOS
self-extractors and patching utility were not launched.

The actual original code agrees with the recipe. At file offset 96,067, bytes
`7d 03` enter a CSI-q payload-read path when at least two parameters are present.
With second parameter 4, that path makes 20 calls to the timed receive routine.
Each empty-buffer call can wait 36 BIOS clock changes, producing roughly 40
seconds of delayed interaction when the expected payload does not arrive.

`check_ansi_freeze.py` executes the original handler and receive routine in a
16-bit Unicorn CPU with controlled BIOS clock changes. The two-parameter
baseline makes 20 receive calls and advances 740 simulated BIOS ticks. The
historical two-NOP replacement makes no receive calls and reaches the handler
epilogue immediately. One-parameter q cases also return normally.

The same harness runs the original status and cursor-position query handler
through modeled UART input/output. Both baseline and candidate return
`ESC [ 0 n` for CSI 5n and `ESC [ 10 ; 20 R` for CSI 6n at the chosen cursor
position. PCPlus already implements those terminal responses; treating all
modern BBS detection failures as missing cursor-position support would be wrong.

The candidate is a partial source rebuild within the original executable container.
It reassembles 1,145 bytes of serial code and applies the historical fix; the
remaining program still comes from the preserved original:

- File: `../reconstruction/dist/tech-net-candidate/PCPLUS.EXE`
- SHA-256: `06708fec7663ad2122ca37947d45e88f4f5766ad70f99f40bac6340a15fa8a00`
- Changed file offsets: 96,067 and 96,068 only
- Source patch: `../reconstruction/patches/tech_net.asm`
- Build/test command, inside the Nix environment: `python3 reconstruction/build_compat.py`

The handler replay begins with parsed CSI state. A separate full-DOS harness
now tests the complete application through DOSBox-X's UART and keyboard. It
compiles an ASPECT startup script using the original ASPCOMP.EXE, starts PCPlus,
sends terminal queries through a loopback TCP peer, injects emulated keyboard
events and verifies return to DOS. The original stops replying after CSI-q and
recovers when the peer supplies its expected payload; the candidate replies
immediately. Both pass status/cursor queries and key translation.

| Executable | Transport | Configured baud | CPU cycles | Result |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Original 2.01 | Raw emulated serial | 9,600 | 6,000 | Expected lockup/recovery reproduced; other checks pass |
| Candidate | Raw emulated serial | 9,600 | 6,000 | Pass |
| Candidate | Raw emulated serial | 38,400 | 6,000 | Pass |
| Candidate | Raw emulated serial | 115,200 | 3,000 | Pass |
| Candidate | Hayes modem with Telnet filtering | 38,400 | 6,000 | Pass |

The modem case issues ATZ, ATNET1 and ATDT to the emulated modem, then checks
binary/echo/suppress-go-ahead negotiation and the same terminal/key behavior.
DOSBox-X consumes server WILL options without replying; the test checks its
supported DO responses. ASPECT PAUSE was found to delay terminal input handling
while the startup script runs, so the script ends before host-side tests begin.
The configured baud tests do not measure sustained throughput or physical UART
reliability. No physical Wi-Fi modem or public BBS was contacted. This is a
concrete fix for one known failure, not proof it matches the user's failure.
The candidate has not been installed on the card.

Run the interactive sandbox with `./tools/pcplus-run` from the project root.
It maintains a private install under `reconstruction/lab/interactive/drive`,
rebuilds the candidate, configures COM1/38,400/8N1/ANSI and enables the emulated
modem's Telnet filtering. Type `ATDThost:port` to connect; Alt-X exits. Incoming
modem listening is disabled. The launcher itself passed a bounded headless
startup/compile/exit test. `./tools/pcplus-test test` reproduces the original vs
candidate regression; `./tools/pcplus-test test-modem` exercises Hayes/Telnet.

The archive also contains keyboard, escape timing and UART-specific fixes.
`archived-support/patch-audit.json` compares their prescribed replacement bytes
against this baseline without applying them. The selected keyboard/timing/FIFO
replacement bytes are absent. One recipe uses unsupported audit commands and is
explicitly marked unknown. A blanket patch collection is not a sensible target:
several fixes deliberately change behavior for particular UARTs or CPU timing.

## Why pseudocode cannot simply be compiled

The original resident export includes 48 pseudocode functions containing
bad-instruction warnings. More subtly, Ghidra removes the BIOS timeout path in
function 0x15ca0 as unreachable: it does not model asynchronously changing BIOS
memory. Compiling that pseudocode literally would turn a finite receive wait
into an endless wait. The observed assembly retains the correct timer behavior.
That routine has now been hand-reconstructed and reassembled exactly.

The native code also relies on real-mode segment relationships: startup sets
DS equal to SS, and assembly helpers use that small-model invariant to access
stack arguments through BX. Overlay lifetime, volatile BIOS/UART state, calling
conventions, relocation records and fixed-address data need explicit recovery.
The synthetic overlay images expose those bytes for static analysis, but their
trampoline substitutions and entry anchors are analyst-created context, not
original runtime behavior. They must never be executed or deployed.

## Practical route to a maintained version

Continue reconstructing the serial driver, keyboard translation and VT/ANSI
parser in bounded units. Preserve the current memory/overlay layout while
reassembling original routines, attach captured serial streams and explicit
regressions to any behavior change, and expand the linked source build as
calling conventions and data structures are recovered. Open Watcom provides a
working DOS C compiler; it has not been established as the original compiler.

A full source rebuild and physical modem/public-BBS validation remain
open. The next diagnostic input is the exact modem model/firmware and a failing
BBS/key sequence, so the next change targets an observed incompatibility.

## Nix and global REA

`../nix/flake.lock` pins Nixpkgs, and the npm lock plus fixed-output hash pin
REA 6.5.0. The environment supplies Ghidra 12.1.2, JDK 21, Open Watcom V2,
NASM, Python with Unicorn, Lhasa and DOSBox-X. Use `../tools/dev` from the project
root as `./tools/dev`; see `../nix/README.md` for individual analysis commands.
The full shell and Nix flake checks have been verified.

Global `rea` and `rea-agents` launchers report 6.5.0 and forward to the user's
Nix profile. The Codex registration points to that launcher; the matching REA
skill is version 42. Existing connected MCP processes keep their old version
until reconnection. This work used a separate verified 6.5.0 MCP session, whose
server identity is preserved in `pcplus-main/binary_session.json`.

The original wrapper, Node launchers, Codex config and skill were backed up
before migration. Earlier npm/provider files remain available for rollback.
The mounted card's PCPLUS.EXE still matches the original SHA-256.

## Independent source link milestone

The dedicated project is now `bstar/pcplus-recomp`. The recovered UART source
supports OMF linking with named state and service symbols while the flat mode
still reproduces the original 1,099 bytes exactly. Its ISR data segment is a
linker relocation, replacing the baseline-only segment literal in this mode.
The separate 46-byte receive timeout remains verified in the compatibility path.

`standalone/serial.asm`, `data.asm` and `services.asm` provide a new DOS host,
new state storage and explicit minimal host callbacks. NASM and Open Watcom link
`build/standalone/SERIAL.EXE` without reading the original executable or data.
The host establishes SS=DS before calling recovered routines. This is an
independent serial diagnostic, not the full PCPlus application or its UI.

All three DOSBox-X cases pass: flow off, software flow and hardware flow modes.
Each echoes more than 4,096 bytes, crosses the receive-ring boundary and verifies
DOS exit, restored IRQ vector and ring invariants. The software case also checks
XOFF pause and XON resume. Hardware mode uses the emulator's asserted CTS;
CTS stall/recovery and physical UART validation remain open. Summaries and exact
binary hashes are committed in `../docs/validation`; full local logs are ignored.
See `../docs/UART.md` for calling conventions and inherited limitations.

## Driver edge cases and ANSI parameter recovery

The maintained OMF driver now has controlled replay coverage for receive
watermarks, overflow in all three flow modes, CTS recovery, bounded output under
CTS/THRE/XOFF stalls, DOS-second rollover and UART/vector restoration. The tests
reproduced an original hardware-flow overflow (count 4104 after eight excess
bytes). Source-only builds guard every ring insertion, count drops and drain
excess input. XON/XOFF transmission is queued for the foreground instead of
waiting inside the ISR. The diagnostic now uses a bounded write API and remains
responsive during output stalls. The exact baseline build is preserved.

The overlay-12 ANSI parameter reader at CS:e3f2 was recovered as 175 bytes of
NASM source and verified against original file offset 94370. The compatibility
build now reassembles 1,320 total bytes across three units; its final executable
still differs from the original only at the historical two-byte CSI-q patch.
This parameter reader is not yet an independently linked complete parser.
See `../docs/ANSI.md` and `../PLAN.md` for remaining work and evidence limits.

## Independent parser and keyboard units

The ANSI parameter reader now links as OMF together with the recovered 16-byte
transition helper, a checked decimal converter and an explicit memory input host.
`PARSER.EXE` passes linked CPU regressions and built-in DOSBox-X checks. Eleven
normal cases agree with the original parameter/decimal/transition instructions;
four deliberate differences reject a reproduced saved-frame overwrite, parameter
count overwrite, word overflow and incomplete input at timeout. The full escape
entry was traced through REA, but its CSI dispatcher and screen integration are
not yet reconstructed. Details and exact evidence are in `../docs/ANSI.md`.

Nine resident keyboard routines (231 bytes across four original ranges) now link
into `KEYBOARD.EXE`. CPU tests cover BIOS selection, normalization, queue state
and callback gating; DOSBox injects k, Up, Right and Alt-X through the actual BIOS
path. The queue producer, terminal-specific maps and full event loop remain open.
See `../docs/KEYBOARD.md`. The original comparison build now reassembles 1,567
bytes across serial, parser and keyboard units, with unchanged final candidate
hash and the same two-byte historical patch.

`../docs/FEATURES.md` inventories the broader application with 16 acceptance
gates, including other emulations, transfers, ASPECT, Host mode, resource/config
formats, DOS integration and memory behavior. Advertised features are not marked
implemented from strings or help text. The complete source rebuild remains open.

lardratboy-fallout-decomp-ports-sdl-read.text:
# FallOut — modern port

A port of the reconstructed FallOut source to current systems (macOS,
Linux, Windows). `src/fallout.c` and `src/gfx.c` are compiled **unmodified**:
a platform layer stands in for DOS, the BIOS and the Turbo C library, the
same way the differential-test harness in `tools/emu/` does.

Status: **milestone 4** — playable with sound (video, keyboard, real-time
clock, PC speaker), high scores saved in `FALLOUT.HIS`.

## Build

Needs CMake ≥ 3.16, a C compiler and Python 3 (used at build time to
generate the compiled copy of `fallout.c`).

```
cmake -S ports/sdl -B build/sdl -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build build/sdl -j8
ctest --test-dir build/sdl          # unit tests + replay parity
build/sdl/fallout                   # play
```

SDL3 is built from a pinned release (3.4.18, SHA-256 checked) and linked
statically, so the binary needs nothing beyond the OS. The first configure
downloads it. To build offline, set `FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_SDL3` to an
unpacked SDL3 source tree. `-DFALLOUT_SYSTEM_SDL=ON` links an installed SDL3
instead.

## Playing

The game's own keys are listed on its About screen (`A` in the main menu).
The port adds:

| Key | |
|---|---|
| F11, Alt+Enter, Cmd+Ctrl+F | fullscreen on/off |
| F12 | 4:3 picture (like a CRT) ↔ square pixels with integer scaling |
| Esc (during play) | pause, like `P` (the original's boss key ran a DOS command) |
| closing the window, Cmd+Q | quits as F10 does, but saves the high scores; a second request quits at once |

Keypad digits always act as digits (NumLock on), which the game treats like
the arrow keys. Keys pressed with Alt or Cmd never reach the game.

Options: `--fullscreen`, `--scale N` (window size N × 320×240, default 3),
`--square`, `--seed N` (fixed random seed), `--volume N` (0–100, default 50;
0 opens no audio device), `--hiscores FILE` (see below). `--help` lists them. The game's own `S` key turns
its sound on and off.

### High scores

The table is kept in `FALLOUT.HIS` in the user's data folder:

| | |
|---|---|
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/bradptaylor/FallOut/` |
| Linux | `~/.local/share/bradptaylor/FallOut/` (or `$XDG_DATA_HOME`) |
| Windows | `%APPDATA%\bradptaylor\FallOut\` |

`--hiscores FILE` uses another file instead. The file is the DOS one, byte for
byte, so a `FALLOUT.HIS` from the original game can be copied in, and back.

As on DOS, the game reads the file at start-up and writes it when you quit
with `Q` in the main menu. F10 quits without saving, as it always did.
Closing the window also quits like F10, but the port saves the table first,
so a window close does not lose the session's scores. The new file is written
next to the old one and then renamed over it.

### Timing

The game is a DOS program that spins in loops. The port uses its calls into
the machine to pump events, draw and sleep:

* The clock is the BIOS tick count (18.2 Hz) since start. It never wraps at
  midnight; the original can stall when it does.
* A loop that keeps reading the same tick sleeps until the next tick or the
  next 70 Hz retrace, whichever is first. A key press wakes it at once.
* Loops that only poll the keyboard (pause screen, difficulty menu) ran as
  fast as the CPU allowed on the original. Here they advance once per 70 Hz
  retrace, mode 13h's refresh rate.
* `delay()` sleeps for exactly the requested time.
* The screen is redrawn when the frame buffer changes, at most once per
  display refresh. An idle game uses about 1–2% of a core.

### Sound

The game plays the PC speaker through Turbo C's `sound()`, `nosound()` and
`delay()`. `src/speaker.c` models what that did to the hardware (EXE offsets
0x7110 and 0x713C):

* `sound()` with the speaker off starts PIT channel 2 in mode 3, a square wave
  that starts high. An odd divisor N is high for (N+1)/2 clocks and low for
  (N−1)/2.
* `sound()` with the speaker already on only writes a new count. The 8254
  loads it at the end of the current half-cycle, so sweeps have no breaks.
* `sound(f)` with f ≤ 18 does nothing; `nosound()` drops the output at once.

Each sample is the exact fraction of its interval for which the output was
high, so even microsecond pulses come out right (the end-of-game tally makes
some). A gentle low-pass (8 kHz) and a DC-blocking high-pass (40 Hz) then
shape it like a small speaker. Samples are rendered at the device's own rate.

`src/audio.c` stamps every speaker change with the time the game made it,
renders up to "now" and queues the samples on an SDL audio stream. The queue
is the latency: the device buffer (512 frames) plus 20 ms, about 30 ms in all.
The sound card and the system clock drift apart, and the queue can run dry if
the game thread stalls. Both are corrected only after the speaker has been off
for longer than the queue is long, when everything queued is silence.

The original's `delay()` counted PIT clocks (1193 per ms) and nothing else ran.
Here a delay can overrun, for example while a frame is presented. While the
speaker sounds, its clock leaves the overrun out, so a 1 ms beep lasts 1 ms;
once the speaker is off, the speaker clock catches up with silence.

## How it fits together

```
src/fallout.c ──tools/emu/mkport.py──> fallout_port.c ─┐
src/gfx.c ──────#include──> src/gfx_port.c ────────────┼──> fallout
shim/ (dos.h conio.h io.h fo_prefix.h)                  │
src/machine.c  far memory, registers, INT 10h/1Ah/21h   │
src/tclib.c    Turbo C rand/srand, exit, system, files  │
src/replay.c   deterministic backend + trace            │
src/rt.c       realtime backend: clock, pacing, keys    │
src/video.c    window, palette, scaling                 │
src/speaker.c  PIT channel 2 → samples                  │
src/audio.c    SDL audio stream, latency ───────────────┘
```

* **`tools/emu/mkport.py`** (shared with the test harness) packs the
  uninitialised globals into one struct in their original order, so the
  original's reads past array ends hit the same neighbours (rotating on the
  bottom row reads `shell_cmd` through `board[17][col]`). It also applies three
  16-bit arithmetic patches where Turbo C's 16-bit `int` makes a difference.
  The one that matters in play is `bonus`: the end-of-game tally adds up to
  1000 per level, and on DOS that wraps at 65536. Finally, it gives
  `struct hiscore` its DOS layout (packed, 32-bit score, 16-bit slot), so the
  table is the 140 bytes of `FALLOUT.HIS` and is read and written unchanged.
* **`shim/fo_prefix.h`** is force-included into the game. It redirects
  `rand`/`srand` to Turbo C's generator. The host `rand()` would break the
  game, because it returns values up to 2³¹−1 and the game scales by 32767.
  It also redirects `exit`, `system`, `open`, `creat` and `close` to the
  platform, and renames the game's `shutdown()` so it cannot capture the
  POSIX socket call.
* **`src/gfx_port.c`** includes `src/gfx.c` and replaces the four routines that
  pass a buffer to the BIOS/DOS as `_DX = (unsigned)ptr`. On a 64-bit host that
  cast loses the pointer, so the replacements pass it in `shim_ptr` instead.
* **`src/machine.c`** implements the DOS machine. Anything that depends on how
  the game is being run goes through a `struct backend`.
* Compiler flags for the game: `-fsigned-char` (Turbo C's `char` is signed),
  `-fwrapv`, `-fno-strict-aliasing`.

## Keeping it faithful

`fallout --harness SCRIPT TRACE SEED [MAX_TICKS]` runs the game against the
same deterministic BIOS/DOS model as `tools/emu/harness.c` and
`tools/emu/run_original.py`. It takes the same environment variables
(`TICK_DIV`, `NO_VGA`, `ALLOC_FAIL`, `HIS_FILE`, `DUMP_TICKS`,
`SHOT_TICKS`/`SHOT_DIR`) and writes the same trace: a CRC of the frame buffer
plus score, level, bonus and total at every clock read and `delay()`, and
every `sound()`/`nosound()` call. Without `HIS_FILE` there is no
`FALLOUT.HIS`; with it, the game reads that file and every write to the file
is traced as hex (the file itself is left alone).

* `tests/parity.sh` replays every `tests/*.keys` script and checks each trace
  against the **original executable's** trace. `tests/t_his_*.keys` load
  crafted tables (`tests/his/mkhis.py`) and check the bytes the game saves. It compares SHA-256 hashes from
  `tests/golden.txt`, so no emulator is needed, and also compares byte for byte
  when `build/difftest/*.orig.trace` exists. The same binary and platform code
  serve both the replay and the game.
* `tests/mkgolden.sh` regenerates `golden.txt` after `tools/emu/run_all.sh` has
  produced fresh original traces.
* `port_unit` (`tests/test_port.c`) covers what replay cannot reach: the key
  map, the BIOS clock maths and the speaker (waveform clock by clock, reloads
  while sounding, area sampling, a filtered 1 kHz tone).
* The realtime build can be scripted for smoke tests: `--keys SCRIPT` types a
  key script's bytes at real BIOS ticks, and `--shot TICK:FILE.bmp` saves the
  window. Headless:
  `SDL_VIDEO_DRIVER=dummy SDL_RENDER_DRIVER=software build/sdl/fallout --keys …`
  Add `SDL_AUDIO_DRIVER=disk` to record the sound to `sdlaudio.raw` (float,
  stereo, at the rate SDL reports). Set `SDL_AUDIO_DEVICE_SAMPLE_FRAMES` to
  1/100 of that rate: the disk driver sleeps in whole milliseconds.
* To compare against the emulated original directly:
  `NATIVE_BIN=build/sdl/fallout NATIVE_ARGS=--harness tools/emu/difftest.sh tests/smoke.keys`

; Batman The Movie (Ocean, 1989) - panel / score routines (resident), all versions
; Module panel: panel.bin, loaded at $6b800, in scenes front, level1, level2, level3, level4, level5.
; Size: RETAIL_2DISK 6268 bytes, RETAIL_1DISK 6145 bytes, BUDGET_1DISK 6176 bytes.
;
; Resident panel module.  Entry points $6b800-$6b870 are a jump table the
; level engines call; the panel bitmap lives in panel_gfx ($75f00) and is copied to
; the visible panel at $7df00 by panel_copy.  Status flags:
;   panel_flags  bit0 time up / paused, bit1 game over, bit2 life lost
;   game_flags   bit0 music on, bit5 abort level, bit6 level complete, bit7 cheat
;
; Labels are named for what they do or hold; unused_ marks code that nothing
; calls.  A label still ending in its address (tab_ table, dat_ data) is one
; whose use is not known yet.  "; from:" lists the routines or modules that
; refer to a label (documentation only).

	include	"config.s"			; CONFIG: which version to assemble

	opt	o-
	org	$6b800


;----------------------------------------------------------------------
; Panel tick, called every frame by the level VBL/timer handlers:
; counts down the timer and depletes energy.
;----------------------------------------------------------------------
panel_tick:	; from: level1, level2_gfx
	movem.l	d0-d7/a0-a2,-(sp)
	bsr.w	tick_body
	movem.l	(sp)+,d0-d7/a0-a2
	rts


;----------------------------------------------------------------------
; Set the level timer, d0 = BCD seconds.
;----------------------------------------------------------------------
panel_set_time:	; from: level1, level2_gfx
	movem.l	d0-d7/a0-a2,-(sp)
	bsr.w	set_time_body
	movem.l	(sp)+,d0-d7/a0-a2
	rts


panel_reset_score:	; from: frontend
	movem.l	d0-d7/a0-a2,-(sp)
	bsr.w	reset_score_body
	movem.l	(sp)+,d0-d7/a0-a2
	rts


;----------------------------------------------------------------------
; Add d0 (BCD) to the score; an extra life every 10000 points.
;----------------------------------------------------------------------
panel_add_score:	; from: level1, level2_gfx
	movem.l	d0-d7/a0-a2,-(sp)
	bsr.w	add_score_body
	movem.l	(sp)+,d0-d7/a0-a2
	rts


;----------------------------------------------------------------------
; Reset to 3 lives and redraw the life icons.
;----------------------------------------------------------------------
panel_reset_lives:	; from: level1, frontend
	movem.l	d0-d7/a0-a2,-(sp)
	bsr.w	reset_lives_body
	movem.l	(sp)+,d0-d7/a0-a2
	rts


panel_add_life:	; from: level1
	movem.l	d0-d7/a0-a2,-(sp)
	bsr.w	panel_extra_life
	movem.l	(sp)+,d0-d7/a0-a2
	rts


;----------------------------------------------------------------------
; Initialise the energy bar.
;----------------------------------------------------------------------
panel_init_energy:	; from: level1, level2_gfx
	movem.l	d0-d7/a0-a2,-(sp)
	bsr.w	init_energy_body
	movem.l	(sp)+,d0-d7/a0-a2
	rts


;----------------------------------------------------------------------
; Lose a life (sets panel_flags bit1 when none are left).
;----------------------------------------------------------------------
panel_lose_life:	; from: level1
	movem.l	d0-d7/a0-a2,-(sp)
	bsr.w	panel_remove_life
	movem.l	(sp)+,d0-d7/a0-a2
	rts


;----------------------------------------------------------------------
; Lose d0 units of energy; a life is lost when the bar is empty.
;----------------------------------------------------------------------
panel_lose_energy:	; from: level1, level2_gfx
	bra.w	lose_energy_body

panel_flags:	; from: level1, frontend, level2_gfx, reset_lives_body, panel_deplete_energy, panel_remove_life, ...
	dc.b	$00
game_flags:	; from: level1, frontend, level2_gfx, panel_remove_life
	dc.b	$00
panel_lives:	; from: panel_extra_life, reset_lives_body, panel_remove_life
	dc.w	$0000
panel_next_life_score:	; from: frontend, add_score_body
	dc.w	$0000,$0000
panel_score:	; from: level1, frontend, reset_score_body, add_score_body
	dc.w	$0000,$0000
panel_tick_count:	; from: add_score_body, set_time_body, tick_body
	dc.w	$0000
panel_time:	; from: level2_gfx, set_time_body, tick_body
	dc.w	$0000
panel_time_bcd:	; from: level2_gfx, set_time_body, tick_body, draw_time
	dc.w	$0300
score_add_value:	; from: add_score_body, tick_body
	dc.w	$0000,$0000
score_drawn:	; from: reset_score_body, add_score_body
	dc.w	$ffff,$ffff
energy_steps_left:	; from: level1, init_energy_body, panel_deplete_energy
	dc.w	$0000
energy_pending:	; from: init_energy_body, panel_deplete_energy, panel_remove_life
	dc.w	$0000
energy_screen_ptr:	; from: init_energy_body, panel_deplete_energy
	dc.w	$0000,$0000
energy_step_ptr:	; from: init_energy_body, panel_deplete_energy
	dc.w	$0000,$0000

; Energy bar bitmap: 41 rows of 32 bytes, copied to the panel at $761c0 (and $7e1c0) by panel_init_energy.
energy_bar_gfx:	; from: init_energy_body
	incbin	"data/pn_ebar.bin"		; $520 bytes of data

; Energy bar depletion: one 32 byte row per step, written over the bar from the top by panel_deplete_energy.
energy_bar_steps:
	incbin	"data/pn_estep.bin"		; $504 bytes of data

; Small digit font for the score: 10 digits of 7 rows x 4 bytes (one plane each).
small_digits:
	incbin	"data/pn_sdig.bin"		; $118 bytes of data

; Blank small digit (leading zeros).
small_digit_blank:
	incbin	"data/pn_sdigb.bin"		; $1c bytes of data

; Time digits: 11 rows x 4 bytes each, offsets in time_digit_offsets (10 digits, colon, blank).
time_digits:
	incbin	"data/pn_tdig.bin"		; $270 bytes of data

; Life icon bitmap drawn on the panel by panel_draw_life_icon.
life_icon_gfx:	; from: panel_extra_life, reset_lives_body
	incbin	"data/pn_life.bin"		; $104 bytes of data

; Blank life icon, drawn over a lost life.
life_icon_blank:	; from: reset_lives_body, panel_remove_life
	incbin	"data/pn_lifeb.bin"		; $10e bytes of data

;----------------------------------------------------------------------
; Copy the panel bitmap from panel_gfx ($75f00) to the screen panel at $7df00.
;----------------------------------------------------------------------
panel_copy:	; from: level1, level2_gfx
	movem.l	d0/a0-a1,-(sp)
	move.l	#$780,d0
	lea	$75f00,a0                       ; panel_gfx +$0
	lea	$7df00,a1
panel_copy_loop:
	move.l	(a0)+,(a1)+
	dbra	d0,panel_copy_loop
	movem.l	(sp)+,d0/a0-a1
	rts


panel_extra_life:	; from: panel_add_life, add_score_body
	lea	life_icon_gfx,a0
	move.w	panel_lives,d0
	addi.w	#$1,panel_lives

;----------------------------------------------------------------------

;----------------------------------------------------------------------
add_score_body:	; from: panel_add_score
	move.l	d0,score_add_value
	lea	score_drawn,a0
	lea	panel_tick_count,a1
	andi.l	#$ff,d0
	movem.l	d0-d1,-(sp)

	andi.b	#$f0,d0
	move.w	#$0,ccr
	abcd	-(a0),-(a1)
	abcd	-(a0),-(a1)
	abcd	-(a0),-(a1)
	move.b	panel_score+1,d1
	andi.b	#$f0,d1
	cmp.b	d0,d1
	beq.s	score_digit_low

score_digit_low:
	movem.l	(sp)+,d0-d1
	move.b	panel_score+3,d0
	cmp.b	score_drawn+3,d0
	beq.s	score_digit_mid

	move.w	#$c1e,d1
	bsr.w	panel_draw_digits
score_digit_mid:
	move.b	panel_score+2,d0
	cmp.b	score_drawn+2,d0
	beq.s	score_digit_high

	move.l	panel_next_life_score,d0

	cmp.b	panel_next_life_score+3,d0

life_digit_mid:
	move.b	panel_score+2,d0
	cmp.b	panel_next_life_score+2,d0

life_digit_high:

set_time_body:	; from: panel_set_time

;----------------------------------------------------------------------

;----------------------------------------------------------------------

	move.w	#$1c19,d1
	bsr.w	panel_draw_digit
	move.b	panel_time_bcd,d0

;----------------------------------------------------------------------

draw_small_digit:	; from: panel_draw_digits
	movem.l	d0-d2/d7,-(sp)

	move.b	d1,d2
	andi.w	#$ff,d2
	mulu.w	#$a0,d2

	move.w	d1,d7
	andi.w	#$1,d7

	asl.w	#2,d1
	add.w	d7,d1
	add.w	d1,d2
